newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks close weak but well off lows.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close weak but well off lows.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed weaker on Tuesday due to nervousness over the outlook for other Asian markets and uncertainty over the local government's future land supply policy, but brokers said the downside was limited.
"We saw across the board selling of blue chips today," said David Williamson, director at Indosuez W.I. Carr. "A lot of it is due to Tung Chee-hwa's comments on increasing land supply."

The Hang Seng Index closed 66.41 points or 0.45 percent lower at 14,792.17 but well off the day's low of 14,686.15. Turnover eased slightly but remained robust at HK$17.57 billion, against Monday's HK$20.02 billion.

Hong Kong's new leader has said his government will focus on increasing the supply of land and housing to curb spiralling prices, although demand-curbing measures such as raising taxes are expected to be avoided.
Regional currency worries and weak Chinese stock markets were also unsettling Hong Kong, brokers said.
"Shanghai is down 3.8 percent and Shenzhen is down five," said Williamson. The Shanghai B share index lost 2.841 points to 71.304 and the Shenzhen B index fell 6.38 points to 121.30.
The downturn in China was due to a hangover of new issues which flooded the market in late June, brokers said.
But brokers said the market was finding a short-term bottom at these levels.
"We saw buying orders coming in at lower levels," said Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities. "The market looks like it will continue to trade sideways."
The index's trading range should remain at 14,600 to 15,000 for the next couple of days, said Cheung.

Utilities were the worst performing blue chips, followed by the commercial and industrial sector. Hongkong Telecom shed HK$0.25 to HK$17.70. Laggard Swire Pacific bucked the downtrend to add HK$1.25 to HK$69.00.
Trading in red chips dominated the market with eight of the 10 most actively traded shares those of China-controlled companies.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index closed 124.54 points, or 3.64 percent lower, at 3,295.95, roughly in line with weakness seen in the Shanghai and Shenzhen markets.
China Resources fell HK$1.40 to HK$34.10.
But petroleum explorer CNPC (Hong Kong), the day's most actively traded issue, gained HK$0.175, or 8.64 percent, to HK$2.20 on trade of HK$1.09 billion.
